newsitem.title: UK: Dollar surges above 125 yen, Euro shares gain.
newsitem.headline: Dollar surges above 125 yen, Euro shares gain.

text.p: The dollar surged to its highest levels against the yen for more than four years on Monday, pushing well above 125 yen in European morning trading to add to earlier gains in Asian business.
Stock markets were also in a positive mood, celebrating a recovery on Wall Street and the strength of the dollar, good news for Europe's exporters.

The U.S. currency, which was also buoyant against the mark, was boosted by prospects for further increases in American interest rates and comments by Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that a firm dollar helped the U.S. economy.
"The dollar is well supported. Perceptions of higher U.S. rates are definitely helping," said a trader at a British bank.
The currency market took little notice of news that Japan's current account balance of payments surplus, a key source of trade friction with Washington, had widened again in February.
"The market largely shrugged off the current account data and everyone is buying dollars," said a dealer at a European bank in Tokyo.

Among key European bourses welcoming a rebound on Wall Street on Friday and hoping for more U.S. gains to come, Frankfurt and Paris jumped around two percent, while London was up a more moderate 0.64 percent by midsession.

Paris share brokers said an informal weekend meeting of European finance ministers on economic and monetary union (EMU) had helped by easing market worries about delays in the timetable for the common euro currency.

But some uncertainty seemed to remain on Monday -- enough to make German Finance Minster Theo Waigel counter press reports that he had softened his stance on the budget deficit criterion for EMU. He insisted that he opposed any looser interpretation of the rule.
The dollar, meanwhile, advanced above 1.70 marks, helped by progress at the weekend meeting towards launching the euro, which would replace the mark.

The German currency also weakened a little against other European units such as the lira and peseta due to renewed optimism on EMU being launched as planned in 1999. It slipped to 986.05 lire from 990.83 late on Friday and to 84.48 pesetas from 84.52.

Analysts said dollar bulls had been encouraged by the lack of acrimony during Rubin's visit to Japan last week when he again criticised Japan's ballooning trade surplus. "The market was geared up for Rubin to talk a bit tougher on trade policy," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas.

On Monday, now in Hanoi, Rubin commented: "I think that the strength of the dollar that we've had for quite some time now has spurred low interest rates, low rates of inflation...in the United States.
"Having said that, I am not expressing any view...with regard to the level or direction that we would seek one way or another," Rubin added.
The dollar has risen steadily since hitting a post-war low just under 80 yen two years ago.
German shares rose more strongly than expected during the morning, catching up with Wall Street's firm close.
"What we are seeing is the typical short squeeze," said one trader, warning that investors could soon take some profits.

The London stock market, Europe's biggest, rose on the back of Friday's gains in New York. U.S. shares in London were mostly firmer as investors anticipated higher levels still when Wall Street reopens.

"The Dow had a pretty good finish on Friday and we should see some follow-through buying in New York," one market maker said. "But if we have any earnings shocks this week, any rally will be strangled very quickly."
The Dow Jones industrial average of U.S. blue-chip stocks ended 48.72 points, or three-quarters of a percentage point, higher at 6,526.07 on Friday.
But for the week as a whole it dropped 214.52 points, the fourth biggest fall on record, as investors fretted about rising U.S. interest rates.
Dealers said lingering worries about higher interest rates and political uncertainties before the British election on May 1 could also prompt caution.
French shares won back ground lost last week, gaining more than two percent at one point in the morning due to the turnaround on Wall Street and the higher dollar.
On other European bourses, Dutch, Italian, Spanish Swedish and Swiss shares were up more than 1.5 percent in the morning.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7010 marks and 125.25 yen, up from 1.6768 and 124.23 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 27.2 points or 0.64 percent at 4,263.8.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 65.94 points or 2.03 percent at 3,310.87.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 46.95 points or 1.86 percent ahead at 2,564.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the morning at $347.85 an ounce, up a little from Friday's London close of $347.45 in thin, nervous trading. Silver added three cents to $4.76.
